district_name: Patricia A. Hannaford Regional Technical School District

jurisdiction_sources.note: 16 V.S.A. section 603(a) inventory: the Patricia A. Hannaford Regional Technical School District, a standalone regional technical (CTE) district under 16 V.S.A. ch. 37, subchapter 5A (sections 1571-1579), serving 17 member towns through three sending districts (Addison Central, Mount Abraham Unified, Addison Northwest).
Patricia A. Hannaford Career Center (official site).

board.org_name: Patricia A. Hannaford Regional Technical School District Board

sources.note: PAHRTSD board page (official, fetched 2026-10-22) labels the seats: the three DIRECTLY ELECTED community at-large seats -- "Vance Bishop - ACSD at Large," "Kim Farnham, Board Chair - MAUSD at Large," "Dan Rossignol - ANWSD at Large" -- alongside the out-of-scope seats (4 partner-high-school representatives and the WIB employer seats). The board structure (11 voting members: 4 partner reps, 3 community at-large elected, 4 employer members nominated by the Workforce Investment Board and appointed by the board; 3-year terms) is the district's standing description via the Addison County Workforce Alliance (https://addisoncountyedc.org/news/join-board-hannaford-career-center). Election model: each at-large seat is elected by ITS OWN sending district's voters at that district's annual meeting -- proven by ACSD's official FY27 Budget Book minutes ("ARTICLE 2: To elect a new ACSD At-Large Board Member for Patricia A. Hannaford"); the RTSD's own warnings never put directors on the district ballot. NO term ends are published for the three elected members (resolving documents: the three sending districts' annual meeting minutes). The voter-approved section 1572(b) agreement itself was not located -- if it provides for direct election of the partner seats, those four seats would come into scope. Only the elected seats are built (Walter's tech-center ruling).

posts.title: School Director (Addison Central At-Large)
posts.note: Hannaford RTSD: the Addison Central community at-large seat, elected by Addison Central SD voters at that district's annual meeting. One of only three directly elected seats on the 11-member board (see the board sources).
